utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. I appreciate the Registry's assistance so that we can continue with the general's evidence today. Mr. Karadzic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to everyone. Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the crisis that we had in August --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear half of what Mr. Karadzic said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Karadzic, could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the crisis that we had in August 1993 [as interpreted], which resulted in the bombing by NATO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say "1993"?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I said "1994." That's what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] I remember a situation in August 1994 in which NATO decided to conduct air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what was the reason for that decision?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason to decide -- to request this air-strike and to grant it was the removal of the heavy weapons from the weapon collection points by the BSA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time, the United Nations or the commanders in the field had to summon NATO. It could not have been only NATO's decision; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. The request for air-strikes was strictly regulated and extended from the requester to the headquarters of UNPROFOR in Zagreb, which ultimately decided whether to transfer such a request to NATO headquarters in Italy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we're going to look at a number of documents to see how the crisis developed. Can we look at 1D2666 in the e-court. And while we're waiting: General, sir, do you remember that you had arrived precisely at the time when an agreement had been reached which would have completely pacified Sarajevo and its environs? And you said yourself that the Serbs were in favour of the demilitarisation of Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to an agreement? I'm not sure exactly which agreement you mean. And the second part of your question concerns a political statement addressing the desire to demilitarise Sarajevo. Now, could you be more specific in your first question? Which agreement are you referring to? And, second, I took note of your remark that the government of the Republika Srpska at the time desired a demilitarised zone, but I don't understand the reflection of the discussion at that time. I have a screen in front of me indicating that the trial started at 9.00 a.m. this morning, but I don't see any text on the screen in front of me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As for the demilitarisation, I think you mentioned, in the examination-in-chief and in your statements, that the Serbian side was in favour of the demilitarisation of Sarajevo, but we will come to that. Do you see before you in e-court a telegram by Ambassador Akashi to Annan, Stoltenberg, and so on and so forth? This is the first page. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's a message of the 8th of February, I suppose. I assume that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at the next page, please. Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that I don't have to read, can you just please look at what General Divjak, with full authority of the B and H Army and government, his army and his government, agreed to as the principles? And if I may just draw your attention to Article E: "On-site monitoring of all BiH weapon system by UNPROFOR. "Sarajevo to become a UN-administered city for a minimum period of two years." And item A absolutely rules out military activities, particularly assaults or attacks. And can we look at the third page now, General, sir. Do you agree that this would have been a very good thing, had it been implemented?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at this page now, please, where Ambassador Akashi is being informed by Michael Rose about his meeting with the Serbian side on the same topic, and General Milovanovic confirmed that he had the full authority from myself and General Mladic to accept these principles. I would like you to look at this list of principles. Do you agree that this is also a significant step from the Serbian side, including the withdrawal of the infantry one kilometre back from the line of confrontation? Would you agree that this was a decisive step in the direction of pacifying the front in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is the 8th of February. If I may remind you, on the 5th of February -- actually, on the 4th of February, there was an incident at Dobrinja, where children were shelled; on the 5th of February, an incident occurred that bears the name "Markale 2 --" actually, "Markale 1," and now we have the initiative being launched to quieten the Sarajevo front. Can we admit this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but we didn't need your submission before you tendered this document. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D830, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 21218, please. 21218.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P1642.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you now to look at the second paragraph of item 1. The whole document can be looked at, but I would like to draw your attention to the date. This is two days later, after that agreement. It's the 10th of February, 1994. The Sarajevo Romanija Corps is beginning the implementation of the concluded agreement. The deputy commander, Colonel, at the time, Dragomir Milosevic is implementing what General Milovanovic accepted. If I can draw your attention to the second paragraph of item 1, where it says: "Should the Muslim side fail to observe the cease-fire and the VRS members are not directly threatened by the fire, do not return fire, but make sure to report back to the Main Staff and officers for co-operation with UNPROFOR." And the paragraph-but-last states: "Enable UN forces to visit our artillery combat positions, and if they find it appropriate to certain positions --" something, "suggests," something like that, and so on and so forth. Do you remember that the Sarajevo Romanija Corps -- actually, you hadn't arrived yet. This is something that you inherited.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document that is being shown now is totally new to me. I've never seen it before. It does give a clear picture of how the orders within the BSA -- how they were executed. In that period, I was not present in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I only arrived on the 24th of February. And looking back, the Total Exclusion Zone coming effectively into action is something which I only came to know after the fact, when I was present in the headquarters from the 24th of February.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. These are steps in that direction. This is why I'm showing this document. Can we tender this? Oh, actually, it's been adopted -- admitted already. All right, very well. Can we have 1D2502 now. I'm afraid that there is no translation, and if there isn't one -- oh, there is one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's quite correct. It will be on its way as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we also look at -- can we also have 1D2503, the translation for that. If that can be prepared, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now look at this document. This is the 16th of February. We're coming close to the time when the Total Exclusion Zone went into force, and the Sarajevo Romanija Corps here is informing its Main Staff about the developments. If I can ask for this -- however, for you to look at: "However, the enemy, under the protection of the forces of the United Nations, deployed at check-points between our units and the Muslim ones is fortifying their positions and they are digging towards our positions by digging up roads at a distance of 50 to 150 metres at a favourable location. They are building bunkers and placing infantry weapons. They are making a departure point for an attack." Can we now look at the second paragraph of item 5, please: [In English] "Please intervene ..." [Interpretation] "Please, by means of this protest that we are sending to the UNPROFOR, we kindly ask that you intervene for the manoeuvring of the enemy to be halted, because in this way we will not be able to keep to the signed cease-fire. The soldiers of our -- the lives of our soldiers are our primary concern." Do you agree that the Muslim Army should not have been carrying out actions like this once an agreement was signed?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, this is not in line with that which General Divjak put in the hands of the BiH Command. I'm not able to say whether this actually reflects the situation on the ground. The report would suggest that what had been agreed by General Divjak wasn't executed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The whole document is interesting. At the end, there's a conclusion, also some predictions, but we don't have time. Can we tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the position of the Prosecution, we'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D831, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D2503 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you've already taken up your duties here and are in a position to implement these agreements. Can you please look to see this is a regular combat report of the 3rd of March, describing the situation up to 1700 hours on the 3rd of March. Can we look at the item marked with the number 3 now, please. It should say "1503 to 1506 hours." This is at the top of the page: "At the time, a UN helicopter was circling over the Lukavica Sector, the Command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, and over the elements of the disposition of the 1st Motorised Brigade. The helicopter was not announced, and it was not approved for the fly-over. We did not open fire. "A UN team controlled the regrouping of artillery weapons (up to 20 kilometres) ..." And so on and so forth. Can we look at paragraph 5 now, please. Do you agree that in paragraph 5 it states that there was six killed and eight wounded after this agreement, and that the commander was having problems to maintain morale because lives were being lost during the cease-fire? And can we now look at the conclusions/predictions. Can we scroll up the text a little bit, please. General Galic is informing here that violations of the cease-fire are continuing. Do you see this report about the violations of the truce? And can we have the last sentence. A little bit down, please: "And regardless of the agreement, the UNPROFOR Command has not shown enough efficacy in its readiness to prevent the Muslims from persistently violating the truce." General, sir, is this proof that the truce was not respected by the Muslim side and that we were losing up to six soldiers even in one day, more than in times when there was no truce?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of wounded and dead, I can neither deny nor confirm. The 9th of February has been quoted. What was the situation, and this was the greatest concern of General Rose, is that from the time that I arrived, from the 24th of February, in the mission area, that the inter-positioning of UNPROFOR units at the confrontation line was a very difficult matter, was proceeding with great difficulty. It was not possible to have Headquarters Sarajevo to take care that the Serbian and Muslim lines was divided by the UNPROFOR units that could prevent conflicts. Despite all efforts, nothing managed to proceed successfully, particularly around the Jewish cemetery. Again, trenches were dug at predicted positions also. I do remember this from that time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have this document admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D832.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have -- can we now have 1D2667.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, do you remember receiving from the Army of Republika Srpska information and protests relating to all these things; in other words, that General Milovanovic kept you apprised of what was going on?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that I did receive information from General Milovanovic about conflicts around the confrontation area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a telegram which pertains to your meeting with General Milovanovic. It's dated the 28th of March, 1994. Can we please look at page 2 just to see what the topics discussed were. I'm not going to read it. Let us just take a look at it. Can we now move to the next page, please. Again, we have the agenda, and item number 3 speaks about heli-flights. There is mention there of an agreement of the 15th of February concluded with General Rose and General Cot, the use of humanitarian aid, helicopters for warring parties, misuse of helicopters, B and H painting their helicopters white, helicopter flights for Casevac and Medivac is no problem. Do you recall that this agreement was reached between the two of you as a kind of achievement, in spite of all the prevailing problems at the time?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: On a large number of areas, we were able to reach agreement in that period so that activities could take place for cessation of hostilities, or to promote such cessation, and to improve the humanitarian situation, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that the Serbian side kept reporting about the Muslim side painting their helicopters white in order to mislead us? That's under item 3, the penultimate sub-item.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was reported. I received no confirmation of this, not even when I once unexpectedly landed at a location where helicopters were standing, BiH helicopters. I did not see any white helicopters. I could not confirm this myself. But what I can confirm is that in discussion on the 27th of March, this was one of the subjects.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, one can see that you agreed to redeployment of two convoys for Srebrenica and one for Zepa, UNMOs on BSA territory. Also discussed was connection between Srebrenica and Zepa, which should not have existed according to the agreement. And then below, incidents, a synchronised action carried out on the 25th of March. And then, again on the 25th of March, the Dutch convoy passed, by force, from Srebrenica to Tuzla without our forces stopping them or opening fire. And, finally, Milovanovic is reporting the cease-fire in Sarajevo is not being adhered to by the Muslims. Do you remember that you two chiefs of staffs had discussed all these issues?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: These incidents were reported by General Milovanovic on the 27th of March and reported to the staff, or in the staff, and reported also to General Rose at HQ, and they were all discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As well as about the failure by the Muslims to honour the agreement?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the time that the Total Exclusion Zone came into effect, General Rose was very much occupied with making this a success, including preventing incidents between the parties along the confrontation line. This was only partially successful. This also has to do with the willingness of both parties to hold to the agreement. General Milovanovic indicates here that the Muslims, in any case, were not following the agreement. And from the Bosnian side, they were also claiming that Serbian units did not conform to the agreement. However, this is not in this report of the discussions with General Milovanovic, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have this document admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D833, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now can we have 1D2511. And I believe there's a translation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree -- yes, here we have the English translation now. Here, again, the Command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps is sending a report to the Command of UNPROFOR or some kind of protest. Can you please look at the first paragraph, which says: "Constant disrespect of cease-fire in the region of Sarajevo by Muslim extremists from the first day of the agreement ..." And so on and so forth. Can you see that paragraph? And below, listed are the most striking examples. Everyone can see for themselves. Do you agree that within a month, up until 21st of April, nothing changed; the violations and provocations -- the violations of truce and provocations continue? Do you remember that the SRK regularly and occasionally reported on truce violations and the impossibility of the truce being sustainable? I have seen you nodding, but you have to give me a verbal response for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once you've finished speaking, I'll give my answer. The general picture, from the moment that I arrived in the mission area, was that there was a great decrease in skirmishes and a great decrease in firing and also in explosions. Nevertheless, on a smaller scale, also, there were many incidents - these were reported - particularly through Sector Sarajevo, which was the first responsible for this, and it would appear that there was reporting taking place directly to Generals Rose and Soubirou. This specific document, I do not remember, but there were repeatedly moments at which both sides reported that the other side was not respecting the agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I please draw your attention to the paragraph which begins: "Since the activities ...," in which General Galic says that the Muslim side is taking advantage of the proximity of your troops and abusing it, and that not even the UN can prevent extremists. This is not saying all the Muslims or the army, but they cannot prevent Muslim extremists in pursuing their intentions. Do you agree and do you know that the Muslim extremists, so to speak, often took advantage of the presence of UN installations to fire at the Serbs and provoke a response that would be a condemnation of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't substantiate that position with facts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. There is sufficient evidence of that. But with the consent of the other side and the Trial Chamber, I would like to offer many, many documents of this nature through Bar Table. Now, can we have this document admitted into evidence? And the submission relating to the inclusion of documents through Bar Table will be provided in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D834, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to skip the documents that are going to be introduced through Bar Table. Could we now have document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the number of the document. Apologies from the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2550. And when it comes to the translation, we are relying on the other side. It seems that we don't have this document translated. In that case, allow me to summarise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a protest sent from the Main Staff of the VRS to the UNPROFOR Command: "Due to numerous violations of truce and the execution of engineering works along separation lines ..." And so on: "... constant activities by the Muslim Army, which is impermissible and incompatible with the agreement which had been in force for several months." Can we now look at the next page, please. Here, again, General Milovanovic, whose name we can see at the bottom, speaks specifically about the engineering works that can be removed in a week's time, and that he is still hopeful that peace will sustain, and he's asking UNPROFOR to undertake vigorous measures. Do you understand -- do you remember receiving such protests?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this specific message. But, in any case, I do know that this issue arrived regularly on the desk of General Rose. And, as I said, he did his utmost to try, through inter-positioning, to have UNPROFOR figure in this, but he wasn't successful in all cases.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have this admitted for identification, or marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D835, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We are now going to skip the whole month, and can we now look at 1D1770. I'm afraid we don't have translation either for this document. So a month later, during which violations occurred on a daily basis, and reports about that were also submitted on a daily basis, but we are going to offer this through a Bar Table.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, we are talking about the 6th of July. The Command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps is sending a secret and confidential report to the Main Staff, specifying which weapons are being used to violate the truce. They are listing infantry weapons, 120 mortar shells. Under number 2, it says: "The fighters of the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade did not return fire at the enemy, in compliance with the agreed truce, and the remaining units did not respond to the enemy's provocations." So we are suffering losses in human life, but also civilians are being killed. Do you agree that the Muslim side should not have done what they were doing and that this constitutes a disrespect or disregard of the concluded agreement?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Retrospectively, neither I nor you are in a position to verify the truth of this document. But if it's confirmed that 120-millimetre shells were used and that's a violation of the agreement that everything over 80 millimetres was regarded as a heavy weapon and should not be used and was to remain under the control of UNPROFOR, and all other subjects, I can't verify whether that's the case, and I don't want to hypothesise about that either. Your Honour, if you permit me, I'd like to make a remark about this. Regarding many of these messages, that it was clear that it was virtually impossible to verify the accusations by the Serbs. It would have been tremendously helpful if freedom of movement and placing of UNPROFOR units on the Serb side, such incidents could have been verified, but that's a retrospective remark. It didn't happen at the time, and we have to live with that fact. So there are major questions as to whether these reports are true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, well, let's say that newspaper reports or some protests sent to you could be perhaps exaggerated, but this is a confidential document, a confidential report sent by the Sarajevo Romanija Corps to the Main Staff. There is no reason for lying in this kind of document; do you agree? Do you believe that the SRK would send a false report to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer that question. As I said earlier, because of the phenomenon that UNPROFOR had no deployments on Serb territory, it was virtually impossible for UNPROFOR to verify these incidents. The veracity, I'll leave that up to the BSA. But verifying the incidents and taking measures accordingly was impossible for UNPROFOR, and I deeply regret that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just one more question about this. From your experience, do you know that lower commands sent false reports to higher commands in the BSA?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the witness has answered that question. We'll mark this for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D836, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Just a small observation: From all the statements given by the general, one may conclude that control and communication within the Serbian Army was such that there was no room for false reports. Can we now have 1D1792, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your submission on statements may not be boring, Mr. Karadzic, but it is not helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, we are approaching a critical moment when NATO launched air-strikes on our forces. I just wanted to show the development that preceded it, in which they were violating the truce and we were the ones who were punished. If there's no translation, allow me to read the first sentence only. It's the 1st of August, 1994: "At 1345, the enemy launched a massive attack along the defence line at Nisic Plateau, focusing at the conjunction between the Kunosici village and Mendzeras Forest ..." And so on. Do you remember that Ambassador Akashi's yesterday's document warned that attacks by the Muslims within the 20-kilometre zone and the Serbs outside the 20-kilometre zone can lead to the Serbs legitimately taking or retrieving their weapons?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to be on the safe side, I'd like to see the document again to see whether that wording is combined with the incident to which you were referring.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Attacks by Muslims inside the 20-kilometre zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please start again your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have to be careful for the benefit of the interpreters. Allow me to read the last sentence, which reads: "We have started relocation of some of heavy weapons which are under control of UNPROFOR as a result of an all-out attack on our defence line." Can we accept -- have this document admitted, which proves that Akashi said that we were right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What was your question about this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the general if he remembers that massive attacks were launched at our forces within the exclusion zones and that the attacks came from within and without the zone, itself; that is to say, from the city of Sarajevo and the areas of the 2nd and 3rd Corps, including Olovo, Visoko, and other places. That was a prelude to the crisis which ended in air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that tense situation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have -- but before that, can we have this document admitted, and can a number be given to it? And then we'll move to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D837.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have D717, please. We showed this document yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, General, could you kindly read, specifically, item 2. And the last sentence states: "BiH activities already prompted ..." [In English] " ... the BSA to seek to withdraw their heavy weapons from the WCPs." [Interpretation] Do you remember this state, this situation?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. Besides, this is a report from 16 August, so at that point the situation had been tense for some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that we had a right to that, to request weapons and to take our weapons which was placed at these collection points?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The agreement that you reached with Mr. Akashi provided for that opportunity. The agreement that you reached with Mr. Akashi on 18 February 1994, if I'm correct. It referred to an immediate attack by the BiH.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at the next page, please, so that we can look at the paragraph marked with the number 3, which actually confirms what you said in His Excellency's telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first sentence says that the legitimate right to self-defence is being recognised; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 3 refers, in fact, to the agreement of 14 February, in which that is again confirmed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then can we look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is our agreement which, I think, is already something that the parties are familiar with. Can we now look at the protocol, which is a part of the agreement. Paragraph 1, if you agree, regulates completely our right to self-defence in the event of the withdrawal of UNPROFOR or in the event of the inability of UNPROFOR to prevent or stop immediately an attack that is underway. The whole paragraph speaks about that. Article 1 is the most important point in the Protocol, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us zoom in further on para 1. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was all asked and answered yesterday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think this was put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I see a reference to paragraph 3 at page 8473, starting at lines 18.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the protocol was insufficiently presented in the courtroom, so I wanted the parties to be reminded, and that the general confirmed that this right of ours existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Isn't that right, General, that this paragraph 1 confirms this right that you also affirmed, and that there is no ambivalence there?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The right to use heavy weapons, again, in the event of self-defence is not contested. What it was about is that UNPROFOR had control of the heavy weapons and that assessing whether heavy weapons should be released by UNPROFOR was a responsibility of UNPROFOR Command; General Rose and General De Lapresle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Lawyers would put it differently, that -- is that that right did not depend on UNPROFOR but on the situation in the field, but never mind. Can we now look at 1D1793, please. Did we request those weapons? Do you recall that conditions were met, from this paragraph 1 or this Article 1, for us to take back those weapons?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember clearly that request. There was a discussion about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If we don't have the translation for this document, will you permit me just to read one sentence: "In the area of responsibility ..." This is this third paragraph. "... ZO of the 1st Sarajevo Motorised Brigade, the enemy is firing with small arms, particularly sniper fire, rifle grenades and mortar shells at our positions and neighbourhoods in Grbavica and Vraca."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that your observers also reported observing mortar shells and fire at Grbavica and Vraca? Do you agree that Grbavica and Vraca are in the center of Sarajevo, that these are Serbian settlements, and that this report speaks about explosions or bombing or shelling of those sections of the town?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember that under -- that there were skirmishes in Grbavica and Vraca. I would like to see reports to refresh my memory. I can't remember clearly all the reports that there were. I think I could only give a positive answer if I were able to see the UNPROFOR reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will show that. I just want to finish with this document. Can we look at the next page. The second paragraph of item 3, it says: "The request was sent to UNPROFOR to take weapons at the collection points of weapons in the north-western part of the corps area. The oral response was negative." So the basic right granted to us under the protocol from Article 1. Can we look at the next page so that we can just see what the situation was and what were the losses inflicted on us. Article 7, "Losses." Four fighters killed, and among them two members of the MUP, and so on and so forth. And then down there, it says: "21 fighters and one civilian wounded." General, sir, what were we supposed to wait for, in terms of self-defence, when, on the 2nd of August -- actually, from the 14th of February until the 2nd of August, the violations of the cease-fire did not stop inflicting losses on the Serbian Army? Would there be any reason for anyone to stand that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before being able to answer this question, I would need to see the request again and the verified answer from HQ, who gave the answer and what were the reasons given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will come to that. The fact is that this refusal resulted in the bombing of the 5th of August. Do you recall that the NATO forces bombed us on the 5th of August because of our attempts at self-defence with heavy weaponry?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. There was a so-called Blue Sword operation by the NATO, an air attack, in order -- on Serbian unauthorised weapons systems within the exclusion zone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be tendered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D838, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that Muslim forces tried to exploit the results of that bombing and that they continued with their firing on the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attack executed on the Bosnian Serbian weapon systems had various effects, and the message that Mr. Akashi sent and which has just been shown, the 16th, refers to that. It could have a consequence if the parties were not to obey the agreements made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Other than firing at the Serbs within the zone, firing from outside the zone, do you recall that the Muslims used heavy weaponry from within the exclusion zone itself, and that you were even angry because of this?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wonder where you have the information that I was angry about something. What is important is that in that period, that is, around the 5th of August, it was clear that non-authorised weapons systems had been taken from the weapon collection points by the BSA and were being used. A similar situation for the Muslim heavy weapons was not found by UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was not found. Let's look at 1D2660, then, please. Had they managed to establish something like that, would the Muslims have been bombed, just as the Serbs were? General, sir, would the Muslims have been bombed just like the Serbs were? We don't need two. One is enough.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, the total exclusion zone regime makes no distinction between Muslim and Serbian units. Therefore, it should, in that case, have taken place in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I agree that it should be the case. Were they punished for violations of the Total Exclusion Zone?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incident being referred to is an incident. As UNPROFOR, we did not see the opportunity to localise -- we did not manage to actually localise the weapons system and take the same measures as for unauthorised weapons on the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you can see here that you're not angry, but you are disappointed. You say, in paragraph 2, that it is very disappointing to discover that especially the Muslims are trying to exploit what the NATO forces did. And in the first paragraph, 847-554 elevation is being identified, the grid reference, meaning that that place could be observed and bombed. But we were not treated equally; is that right, General, sir?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, an attempt was made to actually identify the weapon system. It was able to be established from where shooting took place, but the weapons systems were not found, and that can be seen from the last sentence, which emphasised that the mortar -- that the 2nd French Battalion --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter couldn't hear clearly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ... should attempt to get it into their hands. However, we did find the unauthorised weapons on the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think the interpreter missed some part of your answer, General, probably from "the 2nd French Battalion." If you could kindly repeat that part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The weapons system was not found. It was established, by analysing, from where the shooting came. The weapons system was not able to be attacked. We did act positively, though, in the sense that General Divjak was given the order to place the mortar again under the authority of the 2nd French Battalion, which was active in the Sarajevo area and was active at the weapons collection point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this tendered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D839, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I may remind you, General, sir. On the 13th, you also wrote to Jovan Divjak, and in that letter, you were angry. You said not even 24 hours passed. We showed those documents yesterday and admitted them. Then, again, you wrote to Divjak on the 15th, very angry, because there was firing at Serb settlements from within the exclusion zone. Now I would like us to look at 1D2653 now, please, where we can see all the objections you are voicing on account of the Muslim side. I must say that at the time, you were completely aware of their violations. You are writing this. We cannot see the date. It says "August," and you refer to your letter of the 6th of August. You can see that in the paragraph marked with the number 1, regarding the deliberate violations of the demilitarised zone on Igman, and you are informing him again that their soldiers are continuing to violate the agreement, and then you list all the violations. Do you remember that Muslim forces passed through the zone we handed over to you in 1993 in Igman and killed 20 medical workers in their medical camp? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last incident you mentioned I do not remember. I do remember the letter about a great deal of infantry activity, and which were in contradiction to agreements made, and this is why I used very sharp words to protest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, and you should be lauded for that. But what about NATO, that had more reason to punish the Muslims than the Serbs, but failed to do that? Would it not be necessary, then, to say that they should have been treated the same?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's another comment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I note the time. It's time to have a break. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D840, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we'll have a break for 20 minutes and resume at 20 to 11.00. And you can consult the Court Deputy, how much time you will have after the break to conclude your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to inform the Chamber that this is an exceptionally important witness and that we will not have enough important relevant witnesses for the period dealing with Sarajevo. We're going to have General Rose and some other witnesses from another European country, but I was hoping that I would be given the whole day today so that I could go through documents with this witness that are exceptionally important, dealing with an exceptionally important situation, leaving aside what pertains to Srebrenica, which will require a slightly different approach. But the time that has been given to me until now, we only have 20 minutes left, and I cannot complete what I intended to do in 20 minutes. So I suggest that you grant me the remaining two sessions of today, and I will do my best, if I can, to finish before that. But I really need this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You could have been much more efficient yesterday. That's the Chamber's observation. You'll have until the end of this session, i.e., until 12.00. Do your best, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I accept that I could have been slightly more efficient, but not much more efficient. Anyway, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, throughout this whole period you frequently warned both sides about the events that you were not satisfied with and which constituted violations of the exclusion zone, other than the constant problems of the Igman demilitarised zone, which the Muslims refused to leave; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an impartial organisation, we did, indeed, try to treat both parties equally. I think we succeeded in this, but this does not mean that we always were effective. UNPROFOR's mandate, referring now back to what you showed me before the break, that we could use military means to fight with one or other of the parties in order to force them to respect the agreement, UNPROFOR could only work and only be effective with the agreement of both parties and a willingness from both parties to, indeed, do what had been agreed on. If parties did not respect the agreement, we had to try to convince them. Military means were extremely limited, and this was an obstacle the whole time to UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 1D2658.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you will agree, General, sir, that until the actual use of force, if you were impartial, that the use of force was actually reserved only for use against the Serbs. NATO never used force against the Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my time, talking about air-strikes, air-strikes were only performed against Serbian targets, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recognise this letter of yours? It's true that you do mention both sides here, but this is your letter of the 27th of June, protesting directly to General Delic; no longer addressed to Divjak, but to Delic, General Delic. Can we scroll down a little bit so that the general can look at his signature. General, sir, is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my letter, also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that they would start the fighting in Maglaj and that they were attacking us from Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can neither confirm nor deny who began, but there were skirmishes, with tragic results. Yes, that is clear.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D841, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, General, sir, that reports pertaining to Gorazde about the shooting at the hospital and about 300 dead were exaggerated several times-fold, even 50 times-fold, and that this was something that the United Nations established when they went to Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently, we're going back in time now, the beginning of April, when a Serbian attack was launched from various directions on the safe area of Gorazde, and in that direct fire was involved, tanks shot on a hospital. The number of dead and wounded is something I can say nothing about, whether to confirm or deny it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that after UNPROFOR went into Gorazde, there was an estimate that there was a lot of exaggeration, both in terms of the damage and in terms of the casualties?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: UNHCR had a number of representatives in the enclave at the time of the attack on the enclave. They estimated the number of dead and wounded. General Rose had the impression that it might be exaggerated. After the evacuation, it was established how many dead and wounded there were. I do not have the exact figures, but they can be found in the UNPROFOR records. It was possible later to determine how many there were, and that was able to be established accurately later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you like to look over for a few seconds, less than a minute, in fact, of some footage from Gorazde? Can I have 1D1408, from 14:5:33 to 14:6:43. Can we play this footage. This was admitted during the testimony of General Rose, but I would just like to refresh General Van Baal's memory, to remind him what things looked like and what was the image of Serbs sent out into the world that was actually quite erroneous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "The Reporter: ... instead of the hospital. Only one shell had passed through the roof. As he flew by helicopter into Gorazde following the fighting, Rose was asked about US satellite reports that nearly every house in Gorazde was damaged. "Yes, practically every house in Gorazde has been damaged, but the most of the damage to Gorazde was done in the fighting that had taken place some two years before when the Bosnian Government's forces drove the Serbs from this town. And there were 12 and a half thousand Serbs at that time living here, and they were all driven off. The way to distinguish a house that's been damaged by fighting, where a shell has hit it, and a house that's been damaged by ethnic cleansing, is if it's got not roof, no doors, no window frames and nothing in the house at all, and there are burn marks on it and bullets sprayed around the walls, that is a house that's been damaged by ethnic cleansing. A house that has been damaged by shelling, has a shell hole in it and there are still people trying to live in that building with their furniture because they've got nowhere else to go. That is something that you can't see from satellites. And of course, at that time, the international image of what had happened in Gorazde was very different from the reality. What was dangerous was that policies were going to be put together on both sides of the Atlantic about what we should do in Gorazde, but these policies had been put together on totally flawed information."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with this assessment of General Rose, i.e., that false information were the basis for taking a wrong attitude towards one of the parties to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with the military analysis made by General Rose. Whether this led to a difference in insight in the different parties is something that I would doubt. In any case, it made no difference to the impartiality of UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D2452, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, General, that you were quite successful in dealing with the Serbian side? Most of the things that you requested were granted to you?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the general military situation is concerned, then 1994, particularly when I was chief of staff of command in Bosnia, is the time where relatively there was relative peace and security in Sarajevo and in other parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is one point. And the second point is that we were not successful in really sustainably improving the humanitarian situation. The third point is we did not succeed to bring the former parties in conflict to the negotiating table and to attain a lasting peace. There, we were not successful.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D2452.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for this document: General, somewhere here I have a document containing a joint assessment by UNPROFOR and UNHCR, in which it is said that the UNHCR is achieving 75 per cent of their targets. Another document speaks about the humanitarian aid passing only through the Serbian territory, whereas all other routes are closed. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date and content of the document is something I would really need to see. As I said in my preceding statement, UNHCR and other related organisations, in May and June, were succeed -- were able to succeed 100 per cent in their tasks in 1994. That became less later on. I really need to see that document in order to say whether I had seen it before and whether I could agree to its content.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll show some of these documents if we have time, because some of them are already in evidence. Now, can you please take a glance at this telegram sent by His Excellency Akashi to Stoltenberg and Annan and others. Would you agree that this is a piece of information that relates to the meeting with Dr. Karadzic and Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the title of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, we have a detailed account of the conversation with me that Ambassador Akashi and the Generals Rose and Cot and others had with me. And look at this page, and do you agree that this represents a very fruitful and serious meeting, and do you agree that Dr. Karadzic welcomed the assurance that UNPROFOR's actions would be dictated by Security Council, et cetera, rather than by some councils of various military alliances, and that Dr. Karadzic raised the question requesting specification of the calibres of the weapons to be withdrawn? This is stated under sub-item B. I asked whether we would be allowed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder how General Van Baal can be asked to interpret a meeting that he wasn't even at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Just put your question. We can read the document, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, was this meeting a basis for establishing or reaching at least some improvement during 1994, while you were stationed there?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this document was drawn up after a meeting at which I was not present and for which I had no responsibility. I was not in the mission area, I was not working as chief of staff of UNPROFOR at the staff there. This is clearly a document which then played an important role in the actual execution of duties by UNPROFOR. A number of discussions took place with General Rose at the airport in order to bring the parties in conflict together and to attain lasting peace. In those discussions, it became clear to me that particularly from the Serbian side, Mladic particularly, that there was -- speaking about an overall cease-fire in the whole area of Bosnia and Herzegovina and demilitarisation of the safe zones. This is what I picked up, looking -- just scanning the documents very roughly. But I think this document has a whole history behind it, and it really deserves to be studied properly before I give any further comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But do you agree that at a political level, the political leader of the Serbian side and the political leadership of the UN have laid foundation for the conduct of both parties during 1994? Do you agree that this was the basis for what you were doing in the course of that year?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that in that area, after the Markale incident and the involvement of NATO in the whole process, that there was a great willingness from the Serbian side to come to a final solution under certain [as interpreted] conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please focus on sub-item B, item 4, and the fears that Serbs expressed, in terms of danger deriving from the exclusion zone, the number of the Muslim infantry, the possibility for attacks, et cetera, and also item 5, the UN generals gave assurances that our concerns would be taken into consideration. Do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the end, this meeting contributed to ultimately bringing about the agreement you reached on 18 February 1994, stipulating the rules of play, such as considering implementation of a total exclusion zone. Your Honour, might I also get back to a remark that does not perfectly convey what I said. That's at line 37/2, that: "There was a great willingness from the Serbian side to come to a final conclusion under their conditions." Not "certain conditions," but "their conditions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Speaking of that, General, what would be unacceptable under such circumstances, in terms of conditions that are being mentioned here? Do you know that we always maintained the position that a political solution would not recognise territories taken by force, and that fighting was unnecessary because a solution can be found through political means, and we never said that we intended to keep 70 per cent of Bosnia, if that is what your reference to freezing the lines means?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I meant by "their conditions" was explicitly the demilitarisation of Sarajevo, in part, as well as the other safe areas, and that was unacceptable to the other side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see the next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at item 6, in which General Rose assured me that attacks by the Muslim side at Serbian positions would not be permitted, and that it was also understood that the Serbs would be able to retrieve their weapons, provided they're faced with a massive attack. Do you agree that this is what is written under this item?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take note of the statement provided by General Rose here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that General Galic and Ambassador Akashi mentioned massive attacks on the Serbs, particularly those launched from the Total Exclusion Zone, from places such as Visoko, Olovo, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that you're now getting back to documents showed previously, reporting that later in the year. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You are right. That happened in August. Thank you. Can you please now look at item 8, in which I gave my approval for patrolling operations, and I suggested that UNPROFOR patrols be escorted by a liaison officer and an interpreter to enable the UNPROFOR troops to communicate with the local population, with a purpose of confidence-building measures. Now, can you look at item 8 and tell me that what we proposed was a constructive and a fair offer?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This presentation did, indeed, help to carry out the regime of the Total Exclusion Zone very quickly, so it was helpful.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at the next page. Just one moment. I apologise. Yes, next page, item 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One can see here that the issue of regrouping of weapons is being addressed, and that there are constant threats from NATO, coupled with dead-lines being imposed, and a threat that air-strikes would be carried out against the Serbian positions. Ambassador Akashi here is in concurrence with the Serbian side because he is also keen to see good results achieved.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Is there a question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I was wondering. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic? I mean, you are still complaining about shortage of your time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to ask the general if he agreed with the fact that Ambassador Akashi acknowledged our fears and that he accepted that everything must be done as soon as possible in order to preserve peace and avoid NATO threats. But can we look at the bottom of the page to see what Karadzic asked as an additional request.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at that. Can you tell me, is this a legitimate request, under the circumstances that we are putting our heavy weaponry under supervision, and at the same time our infantry numbers are lower than those of our adversary?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see at the top of the page that Mr. Akashi urges rigid inspections by UNPROFOR, because UNPROFOR had been blamed for being fairly lax about its duties. It was in the interests of the international community to show that this was serious and that the number of weapons systems, and the locations where those weapons were being kept under supervision of UNPROFOR, that this number be minimised. Next, there are a few preambles and finally some remarks, and I would say that it was standard practice among both parties to associate consequences and conditions -- linkaging with their willingness to co-operate. Linkaging was -- the moment they wanted to avoid committing to something, they'd say, Yeah, but you're not meeting our agreements. These boundary conditions basically have nothing to do with implementing the Total Exclusion Zone and taking confidence-building measures, because then that list would have probably been twice the length for both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you agree, General, that this was not posed as a condition, but rather as a request, and that's what is written, and the request for the evacuation of Mount Igman derived from a very firm agreement --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the last part of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Basically, justified complimentary remarks that Dr. Karadzic has raised in his statement, but, nonetheless, divert our attention from the main issue at this meeting. Mount Igman had been demilitarised, and there shouldn't have been any Bosnian Muslim military. And we did our best to reverse this time and again, and several times the effort was not successful, but many times it was. The tunnel underneath the airport was one of the life-lines for survival within Sarajevo for a long period, so that was one point for which UNPROFOR would not take responsibility; namely, closing that tunnel. UNPROFOR would not be responsible for that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. General, we never disputed the right of civilian use of any road or tunnel, but we are talking here about military use. The rest deals with the conversation with Mr. Izetbegovic, but I don't have time for that. Can we admit this into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Don't make any statements, Mr. Karadzic. I take it there's no opposition to the admission of this document, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Of course not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D842, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, do you remember that you found yourself in a situation which was created after the Markale 1 incident of the alleged shelling incident of the 5th of February?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: On 5 February, I wasn't in office, so I'll refrain from any comment concerning the Markale incident, as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But did you talk about this with General Rose, and do you agree that these actions, to a considerable extent, were conditioned by this specific event?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this question is so general that I can't answer yes or no. It was clear that by imposing the Total Exclusion Zone on the warring parties, the violence in and around Sarajevo declined visibly. And, of course, there were all kinds of smaller incidents with unfortunate consequences, both injured and dead, but far less than prior to that time, and that's far more significant than the involvement of NATO in the Bosnia-Herzegovina conflict from 5 February.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you discuss the Markale incident with General Rose?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, as well as the investigation conducted and the conclusion arising from it, which did not determine which of the warring parties could have fired that grenade.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have now Exhibit D162. It's already in evidence. It's General Rose's book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like you to look at one specific passage. Did you hear that the initial investigation indicated that the shot came from the Muslim side and that General Rose issued a warning to the Muslim side? Once we get the book, it's page 65, last paragraph, in e-court.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read General Rose's book, and undoubtedly I've read this page as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you now agree, General, that the Markale incident, instead of aggravating the situation, actually calmed down the situation, and that if it had been done by the Muslims, it was a sort of Pyrrhic victory?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NATO involvement and unilateral imposition of the Total Exclusion Zone by NATO improved the situation, not the incident, as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But look at this: [In English] "The trajectory of the mortar bomb suggested that it had been fired at extremely short range from either side of the line or perhaps detonated in-situ."

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll leave the text in General Rose's book up to General Rose. It's his reality after having left the mission responsibility for UNPROFOR. During my time, I did not see anything about these passages, because they were published only later on, and I was not present at the conversations he's quoting, so I have no opinion on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The previous sentence: [In English] "I told him that the first UN examination of the bomb crater in Markale market-place indicated that the bomb had been fired from the Bosnian side of the battle lines." [Interpretation] And General Hajrulahovic was speechless and anxious. Now, General, can you recognise there was a pattern according to which the Muslims acted in order to lay blame on the Serbs, and they were quite successful in that oftentimes?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to stick to the facts, the facts which I came to know are in a report. The report did not establish -- was not able to establish the -- whether the mortar grenade was fired from the Serbian or the Bosnian side. I don't want to speculate on this or try to work out what the intentions could have been of either party.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can I now ask for 65 ter 2669 now. And while we're waiting, we cannot deal much with Srebrenica. 1D2669. I'm sorry, 1D2669. 1D2669.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that the NIOD Dutch Institute made quite a voluminous study of the Srebrenica events?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Defence is still not unable to -- has still not been able to analyse everything from this study, but there are parts here that refer to you. I wanted to show that to you. So can we please look at page 6 of this document, towards the bottom of the page. May I please ask you to look at this marked paragraph. Did they talk to you, and is it correct, what is stated here, both in reference to the existence of an intelligence service -- does the actual -- the entire paragraph comport with what you, yourself, know?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... intelligence service. Neither did it have assets in order to gather intelligence. The only possibility to gather intelligence was by the troops on the ground, and in my staff we only had limited possibilities for collecting intelligence. We were largely reliant on information on the ground and former combatants who could give us information, but this could usually not be checked. From a national point of view, there were various countries, including England, for instance, which built up their own intelligence service. General Rose had a small group of people, a joint commission of observers, it was called, sort of SAS background people, they were, and from their national point of view, they were supplied information by these people in relation to Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Netherlands didn't have such -- such people and didn't have such possibilities for gathering intelligence, apart from the channels which I have sketched for you just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, since you can read English, the interpreters couldn't hear the first part of your answer because -- due to some overlapping, but could you check whether some part is missing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: UNPROFOR didn't have its own intelligence service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]. [In English] No, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you say, in Dutch --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic be asked to repeat what he said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They "waren bijna allen al vertrokken naar Holland," in Dutch.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a small group of people available to General Rose who could get intelligence. Those people generally had an SAS background.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is what I was thinking of. Thank you. Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this part that is marked and interpret it for us?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, we saw many Americans appearing, including former General Calvin, supreme allied commander, Europe, who was involved in the build-up of the army for the Muslim-Croatian Federation. My British intelligence contacts told me that Americans -- all the Americans had a CIA background. Some of them were in civilian clothes, others in uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The general as well as we can read this document. Put your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, General, sir, was this situation that you described here grounds for concern on our part? Do you suspect or do you believe that we also knew this?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: With respect, the general did not describe that situation. The general has not been asked whether this represents anything he said. In fact, we have no idea what the provenance of this information is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We agree. Move on to your next question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, is this something that arose from your interview from -- with representatives of the NOID [as interpreted] Institute?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. It is paraphrased here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can I ask you to read the last sentence: "According to Van Baal ..."

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement by Rose, this statement is said to be by him. It's quite a few years since I gave the interview -- I had the interview with the NIOD, but I have no reason to assume that it is not as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to information from you, General Rose said that he would agree with the bombing when the American troops are here on the ground, and then he said: "Then I will skip the dual key." Can you explain to us what this "dual key" is in this case?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all cases, the agreement between NATO and the UN was that there would be two approvals along those lines for using air-strikes. It would not be possible that the NATO would independently perform bombings. It was an authority of Mr. Akashi, and later, even, in 1995 of the Secretary-General of the UN in New York and the highest NATO command. That is a "dual key." Literally, "two keys."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at page 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we ask you to look at this marked paragraph, where it says that you suspected that American intelligence officers were operating in Sarajevo and that there were many examples of this, because the American Embassy was close by, and it says: [In English] "'We suddenly saw a host of Americans appear, including the former Saceur Galvin.' According to Van Baal, Galvin had apparently been hired to provide military advice. The interpreter of General Rose and General Smith, Milos Stankovic, refuted this. According to him, Galvin was in Bosnia on a reconnaissance." [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a representation of my observations or remarks.
